intent_en: Putri's hardship represents a much wider low-income population, showing that disadvantage extends well beyond Indonesia's poorest decile.
previous_intent: To illustrate the widespread economic disparity in Indonesia, demonstrating that the financial struggles of the poorest households are representative of a much larger segment of the lower-income population.
narration_support: Putri's story doesn't only apply to the bottom 10 %? Another 68 million Indonesians in the bottom 40 % of households are not much better off.
chart_support: Stylized bar chart comparing household levels, showing a high bar for Dewi's Family and a cluster of low bars populated by multiple family icons for Putri's Family, illustrating a significant disparity and a large lower-income demographic.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states that the situation applies to the bottom 40%, not just the bottom 10%. The chart visualizes this by showing a stark contrast between the top earner (Dewi) and a large group of lower earners (Putri's family and others) on the right side.
sequence_context: Across this sequence, household income inequality places Dewi's family far above Putri's, translates into unequal access to clean water, and affects a broader low-income population than the poorest decile alone.
